subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in `tools.fs` permission policy for user-facing agent outputs, and what boundary keeps internal and sensitive files private?
rationale: The implementation is straightforward only after maintainers choose the product/security boundary for a new config surface that can intentionally loosen file permissions.

options.title: Add a narrow opt-in policy
options.body: Add configurable output modes only for user-facing workspace/tool artifacts while preserving 0600/0700 for OpenClaw-owned private state.

options.title: Keep permissions external
options.body: Document host umask, ACL, group, and container-user setup as the supported path and avoid adding another config knob.

options.title: Fix only specific media failures
options.body: Leave the broad feature open or defer it while addressing narrower bugs such as outbound media upload failures separately.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow opt-in policy
recommendation.body: Add configurable output modes only for user-facing workspace/tool artifacts while preserving 0600/0700 for OpenClaw-owned private state.

likelyOwner.reason: Most connected to recent config/security documentation and current agent runtime internalization among the inspected history candidates.
